title: ledger/v2
description: v2 (2026-10-10, F25-R3; D-23 v3.37): each entry carries `automation`, the structured disclosure its merge's attestation recorded (attestation/v7), or null for an older merge or an undeclared one; `tooling` is unchanged beside it. A v1 ledger is read as v2 with null on every entry and is written as v2 the next time it gains a line. v1 could not be edited (D-34). ledger/<identity>.json (D-19): what one identity contributed, as artifacts rather than as a score. Append-only and bot-owned — every entry is written by the post-merge job from a merge that already happened, so the ledger is derived from the graph's history and never a second source of truth (D-35). Each entry names one of D-19's six lines, the artifact it is, and where it merged; F07 writes two of them, `proof` and `attempts`, and the rest arrive with the features that earn them. There is no weight, no score and no ranking: relative significance is assigned retrospectively at write-up (D-19, D-32), and a ledger that carried a number would be the prospective difficulty scalar D-25 refuses. `status` exists because all credit is versioned and revocable (D-18): revocation flips it and keeps the entry.

identity.description: The pseudonym D-19 says the ledger shows; the network stores no other name

line.description: Which of D-19's six lines this entry is on. F07 writes proof and attempts.

artifact.description: Path of the file this entry is for, relative to the node directory

tooling.description: Model and tooling as declared at submission (D-23); undeclared when the pull request carried no opn-submission block

route_class.description: D-13's class, on an attempts entry only — what makes first-per-route-class checkable from the ledger itself

status.description: All credit is versioned and revocable (D-18); a revoked entry is kept, not deleted

automation.description: D-23 v3.37: the structured disclosure the merge's attestation carried; null when none.

D-23 v3.37: how the artifact was produced, declared by the submitter and never verified. `method`, `models` and `framework` are required of every proof, partial and alternate (the service refuses a submission without them before any pull request opens, F25-R2); the rest is optional, and cost is what an agent can count — wall time, tokens, hardware, a free spend string — never a dollar figure a subscription cannot give.

method.description: Palomar's vocabulary: `manual`, a person wrote it; `copilot`, a person wrote it with model suggestions; `agent`, an agent wrote it under a person's direction; `autonomous`, an agent ran unattended; `other`.

models.description: Every model that contributed, by the name its provider publishes (e.g. `claude-fable-5-1`).

framework.description: The harness or framework the models ran in, with its version where known (e.g. `Claude Code 2.1`).

wall_time.description: How long the work took, in the submitter's words (e.g. `about 40 minutes`).

tokens.description: Total tokens the models consumed and produced, when the harness reports them.

hardware.description: What it ran on (e.g. `one laptop; hosted models`).

spend.description: What it cost, in the submitter's words: `subscription`, `$12.40`, `unknown`.
